title: Share of Counted Payments Taken by the Reinstatement Credit
content:
Patient Services Academy — training note on **Patient Payment Plans**: the share of counted extra-principal payments that the reinstatement credit takes, according to the patient's award under the Patient Financial Assistance Program and the household recorded on the assistance case.

## The rule

The share of the counted payments that the reinstatement credit takes depends on the patient's financial-assistance award and household: for a patient with an approved financial-assistance award and a household of 3 or more on the assistance case, the whole of them; for a patient with an approved award and a household of fewer than 3, three quarters of them; for any other patient, one half of them.

The credit is the counted payments multiplied by the share, taken to the nearest cent, an exact half cent being rounded up, and it is subtracted in the reinstatement payment.

| Approved award | Household on the approved case | Share taken |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | 3 or more | The whole (a share of 1) |
| Yes | 1 or 2 | Three quarters (75 percent) |
| No | — | One half (50 percent) |

## Questions answered (hypothetical; counted payments 84.00)

**An approved award and a household of 4?** The whole: a credit of 84.00.

**An approved award and a household of 2?** Three quarters: 63.00.

**A denied application with a household of 5?** No approved award: one half, 42.00.

**What does "approved award" mean here?** A case of the patient under the Patient Financial Assistance Program whose status is approved; the household is the size recorded on that case.
